facts.statement: Kela can grant general housing allowance to a person who has a small income.
facts.quote: If you have a small income, Kela can grant you general housing allowance.

facts.statement: Kela is the authority that grants general housing allowance, which is intended to help with housing costs.
facts.quote: Kela can grant you general housing allowance. The purpose of the general housing allowance is to help you with your housing costs.

facts.statement: Citizens with questions can call Kela's customer service number 020 634 2550.
facts.quote: If you have any questions, please call our customer service number: 020 634 2550

facts.statement: Kela can pay general housing allowance to one person or to a household of many people.
facts.quote: Kela can pay general housing allowance to one person or to a household of many people.

facts.statement: A household means people who live permanently in the same house or apartment.
facts.quote: A household means people who live permanently in the same house or apartment.

facts.statement: A married couple, a cohabiting unmarried couple or a family count as a household, and one person can also be a household.
facts.quote: For example, a married couple, a cohabiting unmarried couple or a family count as a household. One person can also be a household.

facts.statement: A person may qualify for general housing allowance if they live in a rented house or apartment, a right-of-occupancy home, or a part-ownership home.
facts.quote: You may qualify for general housing allowance if you live • in a rented house or apartment • in a right-of-occupancy home • in a part-ownership home.

facts.statement: A person who owns the apartment or single-family home they live in cannot get general housing allowance.
facts.quote: You cannot get general housing allowance if you own the apartment or single-family home that you live in.

facts.statement: A student can get general housing allowance only if they live with their own child or their partner's child.
facts.quote: If you are a student, you can get general housing allowance only if you live with your own child or your partner’s child.

facts.statement: Kela also provides other housing benefits (housing allowance for pensioners, housing supplement for students, housing assistance for conscripts), described in other guides.
facts.quote: You can also get housing allowance for pensioners, housing supplement for students and housing assistance for conscripts from Kela. These benefits are described in other benefit guides.

facts.statement: Usually only one kind of housing benefit can be paid at a time.
facts.quote: You can usually be paid only one kind of housing benefit at a time.

facts.statement: For a rented house or apartment, accepted housing costs include rent plus water and heating costs.
facts.quote: a rented house or apartment: rent plus water and heating costs

facts.statement: For a right-of-occupancy home, accepted housing costs include the residence charge plus water and heating costs.
facts.quote: a right-of-occupancy home: residence charge plus water and heating costs

facts.statement: For a part-ownership home, accepted housing costs include rent plus water and heating costs.
facts.quote: a part-ownership home: rent plus water and heating costs.

facts.statement: Water and heating costs are accepted as housing costs only if they are not included in the rent or residence charge and must be paid separately.
facts.quote: Water and heating costs are accepted as housing costs if they are not included in your rent or residence charge and you have to pay them separately.

facts.statement: Kela accepts water charges of up to EUR 20 per person per month.
facts.quote: Kela accepts water charges of up to EUR 20 per person and per month.

facts.statement: For a single-person household, Kela accepts heating costs of up to EUR 46 per month.
facts.quote: If you live alone in a single-person household, Kela accepts heating costs of up to EUR 46 per month.

facts.statement: For households with more than one person, the heating cost limit increases by EUR 16 for each additional person.
facts.quote: If your household has more than one person, this limit for acceptable heating costs increases by EUR 16 for each additional person.

facts.statement: Housing allowance can cover up to 70% of housing costs, so the recipient always pays at least 30% of housing costs themselves.
facts.quote: Housing allowance can cover up to 70% of your housing costs. This means that you always pay at least 30% of your housing costs yourself.

facts.statement: General housing allowance only covers housing costs that are defined as acceptable in law.
facts.quote: However, the general housing allowance does not cover all types of housing costs. It only covers housing costs that are defined as acceptable in law.

facts.statement: The law defines maximum housing costs, the highest amount of housing costs Kela can take into account when calculating housing allowance.
facts.quote: The law also defines maximum housing costs. This means the highest amount of housing costs Kela can take into account when calculating how much housing allowance you can get.

facts.statement: If actual housing costs exceed the legal maximum housing costs, Kela uses the maximum housing costs in the calculation.
facts.quote: If your housing costs are higher than the maximum housing costs defined in law, Kela will use the maximum housing costs to calculate how much housing allowance you can get.

facts.statement: The maximum housing costs depend on how many adults and children live in the home and which municipality the home is in.
facts.quote: The maximum amount of housing costs depends on how many adults and children live in the same home and which municipality the home is located in.

facts.statement: Finnish municipalities are divided into categories according to the cost of living there, for the purpose of maximum housing costs.
facts.quote: Finnish municipalities are divided into categories according to the cost of living there.

facts.statement: Maximum housing costs per municipality can be checked on Kela's website (www.kela.fi/maximum-housing-costs).
facts.quote: You can check the maximum housing costs in your municipality on Kela’s website: www.kela.fi/maximum-housing-costs.

facts.statement: Example: for a person living alone in Helsinki, up to EUR 563 per month can be accepted as housing costs; with rent of EUR 800, Kela calculates using EUR 563.
facts.quote: Up to EUR 563 per month can be accepted as housing costs for a person living alone in Helsinki. This means that Kela calculates how much housing allowance Maija can get based on this maximum amount of housing costs (EUR 563).

facts.statement: Example: for a person living alone in Kemi, up to EUR 394 per month can be accepted; a subtenant paying EUR 291 has the allowance calculated on the actual rent because it is lower than the maximum.
facts.quote: Up to EUR 394 per month can be accepted as housing costs for a person living alone in Kemi. This means that Kela calculates how much housing allowance Tommi can get based on his rent (EUR 291) because Tommi’s rent is lower than the maximum housing costs

facts.statement: Income and assets affect the amount of general housing allowance.
facts.quote: Your income and assets affect how much general housing allowance you can get.

facts.statement: Kela deducts a basic deductible from the housing costs when calculating the housing allowance.
facts.quote: Kela deducts a basic deductible from the housing costs when calculating the amount of housing allowance Kela can pay.

facts.statement: The basic deductible depends on the number of adults and children in the household and the gross household income per month (income before taxes).
facts.quote: The amount of the basic deductible depends on • how many adults and children live in the household • the gross household income per month. Gross income means income before taxes.

facts.statement: The bigger the income, the larger the basic deductible.
facts.quote: The bigger the income is, the larger the deductible.

facts.statement: Earned income (e.g. wages or salary) affects the amount of housing allowance.
facts.quote: earned income (for example wages or salary)

facts.statement: Assets (e.g. shares and money in a bank account) affect the amount of housing allowance.
facts.quote: assets (for example shares and money in your bank account)

facts.statement: Capital income (e.g. rental income or interest on deposits) affects the amount of housing allowance.
facts.quote: capital income (for example rental income or interest on deposits)

facts.statement: Various benefits (e.g. unemployment benefits, sickness allowance, parental daily allowances) affect the amount of housing allowance.
facts.quote: various benefits (for example unemployment benefits, sickness allowance and daily allowances for parents).

facts.statement: Certain benefits (e.g. social assistance, child benefit, provider supplement to the study grant, informal care allowance) do not affect the housing allowance amount.
facts.quote: he amount of housing allowance is not affected by • certain benefits (for example social assistance, child benefit, provider supplement to the study grant or informal care allowance)

facts.statement: The income and assets of a child under 18 who is a household member do not affect the housing allowance.
facts.quote: the income and assets of a child under the age of 18 who is a member of the household.

facts.statement: Kela calculates a continuous income if the income will stay the same for 3 months after the allowance is granted or reviewed.
facts.quote: Kela will calculate a continuous income for you in the following situation: your income will stay the same for 3 months after you have been granted housing allowance or after your housing allowance has been reviewed.

facts.statement: If income varies from month to month, Kela calculates an average income based on income for the next 12 months (e.g. for people with short temporary jobs and unemployment between them).
facts.quote: If your income is different from one month to the next, Kela will calculate an average income for you based on your income for the next 12 months. This can be the case if, for example, you sometimes have short temporary jobs

facts.statement: The applicant must declare all of their income in the housing allowance application.
facts.quote: You must declare all of your income in the application for housing allowance.

facts.statement: Kela can obtain information on wages and salaries paid to the applicant from the Incomes Register.
facts.quote: Kela can also get information on wages and salaries paid to you from the Incomes Register.

facts.statement: The recipient must tell Kela if their income increases or decreases.
facts.quote: Remember to tell Kela if your income increases or decreases.

facts.statement: Kela first deducts the basic deductible from the housing costs; the housing allowance equals 70% of the remaining acceptable housing costs.
facts.quote: First, Kela deducts the basic deductible from your housing costs. The housing allowance you can get is equal to 70% of the remaining amount of acceptable housing costs.

facts.statement: A housing allowance calculator on Kela's website can be used to estimate the allowance amount.
facts.quote: You can use the housing allowance calculator on Kela’s website to estimate how much housing allowance you can get. www.kela.fi/calculators

facts.statement: Example: a person living alone in Turku with EUR 800/month unemployment allowance has a basic deductible of EUR 19.50 per month; up to EUR 447 per month can be accepted as housing costs in Turku (the text also states EUR 477 in one place).
facts.quote: Jaakko’s basic deductible is EUR 19.50 per month. Up to EUR 447 per month can be accepted as housing costs for a person living alone in Turku. Jaakko’s housing allowance is calculated on the basis of this maximum amount of housing costs (EUR 477).

facts.statement: Example: EUR 447 minus the EUR 19.50 deductible leaves EUR 427.50; the allowance is 0.7 x 427.50 = EUR 299.25 per month, and the person pays EUR 400.75 of the EUR 700 rent themselves.
facts.quote: the amount left is EUR 427.50. This means that the housing allowance that Jaakko gets is equal to 70% of EUR 427.50. The calculation looks like this: 0.7 x 427.50 = EUR 299.25 per month. The amount of housing costs Jaakko pays himself per month is EUR 400.75 (700 – 299.25 = 400.75).

facts.statement: General housing allowance can be applied for online via Kela's e-services (in Finnish and Swedish).
facts.quote: Apply for general housing allowance online: www.kela.fi/e-services (in Finnish and Swedish)

facts.statement: The application lists the supporting documents that must be sent with it.
facts.quote: Check the application for a list of the supporting documents you need to send with the application.

facts.statement: Supporting documents can also be sent online.
facts.quote: The supporting documents can also be sent online.

facts.statement: The applicant can apply using a paper application form obtained from a service point or Kela's website.
facts.quote: You can also apply by filling in an application form that you can get from a service point or from Kela’s website: www.kela.fi/forms

facts.statement: A paper application form must be sent to Kela by post to Kela, PL 10, 00056 KELA.
facts.quote: If you apply for a Kela benefit on an application form, send the application to Kela by post. Kela’s address is: Kela PL 10 00056 KELA

facts.statement: Citizens can call Kela for help with almost all matters related to Kela benefits.
facts.quote: You can also call us for help with almost all matters related to Kela benefits.

facts.statement: Housing allowance can be applied for retroactively for up to one month.
facts.quote: You can apply for housing allowance retroactively for up to one month.

facts.statement: To receive the allowance from January onward, Kela must receive the application before the end of February.
facts.quote: For example, if you want to get the allowance from January onward, Kela must get your application before the end of February.

facts.statement: After processing the application, Kela sends a decision notice in the OmaKela e-service or by post to the home address.
facts.quote: As soon as Kela has processed your application, you will get a decision notice in the OmaKela e-service or by post to your home address.

facts.statement: The decision notice states the benefit amount, the reasons for granting it, and when it will be paid.
facts.quote: The decision notice will tell you how much benefit you get, the reasons for granting it and when it will be paid to you.

facts.statement: A decision notice is also sent if Kela rejects the application.
facts.quote: You will get a decision notice also if Kela rejects your application.

facts.statement: Kela pays general housing allowance to the recipient's bank account on the first banking day of the month.
facts.quote: Kela pays the general housing allowance to your bank account on the first banking day of the month.

facts.statement: A bank account is needed for payment of the housing allowance.
facts.quote: Kela pays the general housing allowance to your bank account

facts.statement: The recipient can ask Kela to pay the housing allowance directly to the landlord.
facts.quote: You can also ask Kela to pay your housing allowance directly to your landlord.

facts.statement: Kela reviews the housing allowance once a year.
facts.quote: Kela reviews the housing allowance once a year.

facts.statement: Kela can review the allowance sooner than the annual review if the recipient's circumstances change.
facts.quote: Kela can review the allowance sooner if your circumstances change.

facts.statement: Recipients must report changes in life situation, e.g. housing, income, work or family circumstances, to Kela.
facts.quote: The change can concern for example your housing, income, work or family circumstances. Remember to report such changes to Kela.

facts.statement: Changes can be reported online in OmaKela, by phone, or by visiting a Kela service point.
facts.quote: You can do it online in the OmaKela e-service, by phone or by visiting a Kela service point.

facts.statement: It is the recipient's responsibility to make sure Kela has correct information so the right amount is paid.
facts.quote: It is up to you to make sure that Kela has the correct information. That way you will be paid the right amount of benefit.

facts.statement: A person who thinks Kela's decision is wrong can appeal to have it changed.
facts.quote: If you think that the decision you got from Kela is wrong, you can appeal to have it changed.

facts.statement: Appeal instructions are included with every decision notice from Kela.
facts.quote: You get instructions on how to appeal the decision with every decision notice you get from Kela.

facts.statement: Persons with questions about a decision should contact Kela first.
facts.quote: If you have questions, please contact Kela first.

facts.statement: In OmaKela, users can apply for benefits, submit supporting documents, check application status, send messages, report changes, and stop benefit payments.
facts.quote: In the OmaKela e-service you can • apply for Kela benefits • submit supporting documents • get information about the status of your application • send messages • report changes • stop the payment of benefits.

facts.statement: OmaKela is available in Finnish, Swedish or Sámi.
facts.quote: Kela’s e-service OmaKela (in Finnish, Swedish or Sámi): www.kela.fi/e-services

facts.statement: Logging in to OmaKela requires online banking credentials or a mobile ID.
facts.quote: You must log in to OmaKela. You need online banking credentials or a mobile ID.

facts.statement: Help with using e-services is available via Kela's digital support.
facts.quote: If you have difficulties using the e-services, you can get help: www.kela.fi/digital-support

facts.statement: A person can give another person permission to act on their behalf at Kela.
facts.quote: You can give another person permission to act on your behalf at Kela:

facts.statement: Interpreter assistance is available for people who do not speak Finnish, Swedish or English.
facts.quote: If you do not speak Finnish, Swedish or English, you can get interpreter assistance:

facts.statement: Kela's phone service for families, students, unemployment and housing (020 634 2550) is open Monday to Friday 9.00–15.00.
facts.quote: Monday to Friday from 9.00 to 15.00. Families, students, unemployment and housing 020 634 2550

facts.statement: A call request can be submitted in OmaKela or while waiting in the queue during a customer service call.
facts.quote: You can submit a call request in OmaKela or while waiting in queue during a customer service call.

facts.statement: Citizens can visit Kela service points; addresses and opening hours are on Kela's website.
facts.quote: Visit a service point Check the addresses and opening hours of our service points: www.kela.fi/visit-kela

facts.statement: Kela has an Overpayment Recovery Centre reachable by phone.
facts.quote: Overpayment Recovery Centre Monday to Friday from 10.00 to 15.00. 020 634 4940
